## Goal

Projects' own front ends shown as real demos everywhere a page is seen, and every artifact exportable without pretending server features still work.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| TM-08 | Web demos: a project's own front end, built from its source into the version and shown in `<WebDemo>` with device frames, viewport switching and screenshots, the same locally, through any share, on a remote server and in every export | I, B | A Vite app and a Next.js static-export app, each with client-side routing and mock data, build through the demo spec and pass verify; fully interactive in `<WebDemo>` in three engines, locally and through a share; a deep link works; a comment inside a demo survives a reload; a broken build fails verify with its log; device frames and screenshots |
| VR-07 | Export: client-only artifacts to static files or a single HTML file, with their demos, opening from disk; server artifacts to a runnable bundle; any artifact to a snapshot archive with actions marked unavailable; no server code in any export, and what an export loses named | I, B | Each export class produced from fixtures and opened from disk with its demos in three engines; a history-routed demo from disk shows its notice; `static --base /sub/` serves a history-routed demo fully from `/sub/`; snapshot marks actions unavailable; no server code or secret in any output; bundle runs via `mostra run` |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- declared demos (D185: a demo is a built front end, never a running dev server) built from their source at `verify`, publish and on demand (`mostra demo build`), cached by the source's content, stored with the version and served from the artifact origin under `/_mostra/demos/<name>/` with an SPA fallback;
- bridge injection into a demo's documents and its opt-out;
- `useDemo` and `<WebDemo>` with device frames and viewports;
- the `static`, `html` and `snapshot` export classes, carrying demos, with `--base`, `--strict`, `--submission` and `--no-shared-state`, an export report naming what each loses, controls degrading in place, and no server code in any export (the `bundle` class, `mostra run` and the `WorkerLauncher` documentation are WP-29's, D125).

Terminal exports wait for the terminal packages.

Design detail for this package:

- D185 decides the package: a demo is a built front end (Vite, a Next.js static export, any framework that emits static files) built from its declared source at `verify`, publish and on demand, stored with the version under `client/_mostra/demos/<name>/` and served from the artifact origin under `/_mostra/demos/<name>/` with an SPA fallback; no dev servers, proxies, hot reload or server side (D185 items 1 and 2).
- The build (D185 item 4): in its `source` folder, the artifact environment plus `env`, the user's `PATH` first and Mostra's Node.js last, `MOSTRA_DEMO_BASE`; one build at a time per demo folder in its own process group or Job Object, killed with its tree on timeout or cancel; cached by the source's content; `MOSTRA_DEMO_*` errors at `verify` with the build's last log lines; `demoDigest` joins `envDigest`.
- From WP-20 (D183 item 7): the version's review agent (`registry.json`'s `reviewAgent`) is injected into a demo's documents unless `bridge: false`, so comments anchor inside the demo.
- `useDemo` in `@mostra/react`, `<WebDemo>` in `@mostra/kit/demo` with device frames, viewports, `values` and `onMessage`; `verify` waits for demos to load.
- From WP-07 (D111), moved from WP-13 (D158): the `static` export writes `<meta name="mostra-target" content="static">` into `index.html`; the client runtime then routes by hash and keeps fields in local storage, as `tests/e2e/specs/pages.spec.ts` checks on a marked build: run that check on the real exporter's output (AU-09).
- The `static`, `html` and `snapshot` export classes as D185 items 7 and 8 describe them, with the export report, `--base`, `--strict`, `--submission`, `--no-shared-state`, the in-frame notice from disk and the README. The `bundle` class, `mostra run <bundle>` and the `WorkerLauncher` documentation moved to WP-29 (D125), which a share needs first; VR-07's bundle case reuses them.

## Out of scope

- MCP App export (WP-17)
- The `bundle` class and `mostra run` (WP-29)
- Terminal exports (WP-22, WP-23)
- Dev servers, hot reload and demos with a server side (D185 item 2)

## Acceptance evidence

- a Vite app and a Next.js static-export app, each with client-side routing and mock data, build through the demo spec and pass `verify`, with their screenshots;
- both are fully interactive in `<WebDemo>` in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, locally and through a share; a deep link to a client-side route works; a review comment inside a demo survives a reload;
- a broken build fails `verify` with its log;
- each export class opens the demo from disk in all three engines; a history-routed demo from disk shows its notice when it navigates in Chromium; a `static` export with `--base /sub/` serves a history-routed demo fully from `/sub/`;
- actions show as unavailable in `static` and `snapshot`, and an export of a page with actions, a live producer and a secret holds none of their server code or values;
- VR-07's bundle case reuses WP-29's `bundle` class and `mostra run`.

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- Chromium and WebKit refuse history navigation, `fetch` and module scripts in `file:` pages: from disk a history-routed demo works on its opening route only (D185 item 7).
- A Next.js export loads classic chunk scripts by URL, so it can't be carried inside one file (D185 item 7).

## Handoff

J5's embedded demo works everywhere a page is seen; every export class is proven.
